mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units for three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1,000,000 for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease of at least 0.25 percentage points in FEDFUNDS and a concurrent rise of more than 0.5% in CPIAUCSL signals a monetary policy lag, where rate cuts fail to offset inflation, eroding real purchasing power and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls > 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coincident with a decline of more than 2% in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.4% AND PAYEMS falls > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent quarterly increase in real GDP (GDPC1) of at least 2% over two consecutive quarters signals robust economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which raises earnings for industrial firms and supports higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
